name: Pullman estate (1800 S. Calumet Avenue): Beman's conservatory at the head of the north range, K13

function.note: The 1911 sheet letters the range 'GREEN HO.' with a glass roof ('GLASS R'F' / 'GLASS ROOF'), and the sheet-28 census allocates it to the Pullman estate (s28-pullman-service-garden), on the placement of Beman's conservatory 'across 18th Street from the house (toward Calumet)' in the image research; no deed has been read. The pavilion is the cross-shaped head the sheet draws at the north end of the north range.

research_note: T-3164 (piece 1 of T-1934): Pullman's glasshouse ground across 18th Street, which the district draft left empty because the sheet-28 trace never drew it (T-2335, L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335). Read off sheet 28 by hand at the pixels named in each note, as T-2306 read the house's own bay off sheet 20, because the colour trace cannot separate these ranges: the lodge's pink wash spills diagonally across the east range on this copy. Every size above the plan is the K13 kit's reconstruction (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164). T-3165 works the glasshouses to the 1894 plates and the photographs and replaces what they contradict.

documented_range.note: The record claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the sheet-28 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-28.json, allocation s28-pullman-service-garden) rules the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground present in 1904. Its building date, which the census reads off the 1894 conservatory plate, is T-3165's to read from the pictures themselves.

position.symbolic_location: 1800 S. Calumet Avenue, parcel calumet_1800 (data/street_grid/1904.json): the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground across 18th Street from the house, west side of Calumet Avenue between 18th and 20th Streets; its north end, facing 18th Street.
position.note: The north-east corner, read off the committed sheet 28 raster at pixel (3166, 1640) where the drawn wall lines cross, and carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json; 1.47 m RMS on independent standing houses): local E 1468.88, N -3238.36. The bearing turns the plan onto the sheet's own ruled lines (1.014 degrees off east in that fit), so the building runs square to the lot as drawn.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is the pixel named in the note, of the committed sheet 28 raster, carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: From the corner at the origin, u along the range and v across it (v = -z of the kit's plan, so north on an east-west range and east on a north-south one). The drawn wall lines' centres on the sheet (x 3001-3166, y 1640-1889) at 0.0506 m a pixel: 12.59 by 8.34 m. The south end is drawn as a dashed line with a gap, the door into the north range; the plan stops 0.05 m short of it so the two glass ends never meet in one plane.

stories.note: The sheet prints '1' on the glasshouse: one storey.

construction.note: Lettered 'GLASS R'F' / 'GLASS ROOF' on the sheet, over the blue wash this copy gives the whole glasshouse ground. The kit stands the glass on a brick plinth.

conservatory.note: T-3179: Beman's conservatory as the 1894 Inland Architect plate and the Lowe c. 1897 photograph show it from 18th Street, worked through their solved cameras (data/reference_views/pullman_glasshouse_1800_calumet_pavilion/): a glass nave on a pointed (Gothic) section, its north end the plate's great pointed arch, on a stone podium 2.3 m high with a band of upright glazing over it to the springing at 3.6 m and the apex at about 9.45 m; the arched stone entrance 2.4 m wide in its north end, its crown about 3.5 m; a pointed transept 7.0 m wide crossing it at mid-length and standing 1.35 m out each side, its ridge about 9.35 m; and an octagonal glazed drum (to 10.1 m) under a ribbed dome about 3.7 m across, its crown about 12.7 m and its finial about 13.5 m. The plan is the 1911 sheet's (inferred): the long arm's 12.59 by 8.34 m and the cross arms 1.3-1.4 m each side over 7 m of its length, which the plate's transept end confirms within about 0.2 m through the camera. Heights are read off the plate at 49.5 px/m on the north front (its width, 8.34 m, scales it) and agree with the Lowe photograph within 0.2 m. RECONSTRUCTED within that: the vault's eight facets a half, the bays, the transept and dome glazed in the kit's opaque substitute (they stand outside the nave's one transparent envelope), the cresting the plate shows along the transept ridge (under 1 ft, not built) and everything the pictures do not show of the south end (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164, L-pullman-conservatory-3179). T-3164 (owner, 2026-10-28: "the pavilion's great arched glass front as an opaque gable over a black opening"): the north front's band between the podium and the springing is drawn as the Lowe photograph shows it, round-headed lights in white framing, four each side of the entrance, and three along the east flank north of the transept, the flank both pictures see; the conservatory's planted depth is drawn in shade inside the nave to about 5.2 m, so the glass reads dark over the lower half of the arch with the roof's light over it, as both pictures read it. RECONSTRUCTED: the lights' count (read off the photograph's north front), the interior as one shaded volume and not a planted scene; the west flank's band, which neither picture sees, is left as the kit's glass, the house being at its triangle budget (L-pullman-pavilion-front-3164). T-3164 (the match records' open differences, 2026-10-29: "the nave's arch is a smooth curve; the render's is four planar facets a half" and "iron cresting along the transept's crest ... and the small ornaments at the nave's apex and the transept's end"): the vault, the transept's section and the dome are drawn in eight facets a half (the dome in eight rings), so the pointed arch reads as the plate's smooth curve: on this 8.34 m span (radius 6.19 m) eight facets leave a chord at most 0.019 m inside the true arc, under the kit's own 0.02 m max_sag_m for a curved roof, where four left 0.074 m; an iron cresting 0.3 m high, pickets every 0.15 m between a foot and a top rail, runs along each transept arm's level crest from its hipped end to the nave, with a 0.6 m finial over each arm's end and a 0.4 m finial over the north arch's point, all in the frame's paint, as the plate draws them light against the sky. RECONSTRUCTED: the cresting's pattern (the plate resolves a light lattice about a foot high, not its design) and the finials' heights, read against the dome's 0.5 m finial in the same plate (L-pullman-pavilion-curves-3164). T-3164 (the match records' open difference, 2026-10-29: "the transept arms' lights have round heads and tracery (drawn square-headed)"): the transept arms' band between the podium and the springing is drawn as both pictures show it on the east arm, tall lights under a transom 0.38 m below the head, each with a short round-headed light over it, in white framing, about 0.45 m a light, so three across each arm's side as both pictures count them. RECONSTRUCTED: the ends' and the west arm's lights, which neither picture sees face on, carried round at the side's spacing, and the heads' tracery drawn as one pane (L-pullman-transept-band-3164). T-3164 (the match records' open difference, 2026-10-29: "the dome and its drum stand about 25 px (0.6 m) west of the plate's"): re-read through both solved cameras, the dome's finial stands at x 1370 on the Inland plate and x 896 in Lowe's print, which on the nave's axis put the dome's centre at u 4.45 and 4.5, 1.8 m north of the transept's middle (u 6.3, held by the 1911 sheet's cross arms and the plate's transept end), so the drum and dome stand at u 4.5 (drum.centre_m) and the transept is left where it fits. Read again at that depth: the drum's top at 9.7-9.8 m (built 9.75; it was 10.0), the dome's crown at 12.3 m on the plate and 12.7 m in Lowe (built 12.5, a 2.75 m rise; it was 13.1) and the finial's tip at 13.6-13.8 m, the finial a turned iron ornament in both pictures, a flared foot about 0.6 m across, a bulb, a neck, a knob and a spike (built to that profile, 1.3 m; it was a 0.5 m stick). RECONSTRUCTED: the finial's profile, read at about 0.02 m a pixel off the plate, and the dome's place across the nave, held on its axis because neither picture can tell a shift across from one along (L-pullman-dome-place-3164). T-3164 (gate pass): the estate's gate on 18th Street in the plate's foreground (Lowe's print shows it too), built on this record because the drive it opens leads to this entrance and the grounds have no record of their own: two square stone piers 0.8 m on a 0.3 m plinth under a three-course cap to 2.2 m, and from each a wing returning 1.15 m along the street line toward the drive, its top sweeping down from 1.1 m at the pier to a scroll's roll at 0.76 m over a 0.55 m block at the drive's edge. Placed and sized through the plate's solved camera (whose eye height was set on the walk's back at these piers): the bases' fronts read at u -22.1 and -21.5 (set at -21.8, about 0.6 m inside the lot's 18th Street line), the west pier's east face at v 4.09 and the east pier's west face at v 10.49, the drive 4.1 m between the wings' ends; heights read at 111 px/m. RECONSTRUCTED within that: the cap's courses and the sweep's curve drawn plain, the stone taken as the podium's (the piers' lit faces read its tone), and the carved panel on each wing's face and the sunk panel on each pier not built (L-pullman-gate-1800-calumet-3164). T-3164 (the match records' open difference, 2026-10-29: "the carved scroll panel on each wing's street face and the sunk panel on each pier's faces"): read off both pictures through their cameras, each wing's street face carries a spiral C-scroll about 0.26 m across by the pier (its centre 0.28 m along the wing and 0.76 m up), three lobes of leafage trailing from it under the sweep toward the roll, and a fillet over the plain base at 0.48-0.53 m, all 0.05 m proud (gate.carving); each pier's shaft carries a sunk panel 0.08 m in from its edges between 1.24 and 1.8 m, sunk 0.05 m (gate.panel). RECONSTRUCTED: the leaves' cutting and count and the relief's depth, which neither picture resolves; the panels carried round the two faces neither picture sees; the wings' garden faces left plain (L-pullman-gate-1800-calumet-3164).
